title: Device Delta Profiles and Pin-Decay Recommendations for Cross‑SKU Onboarding
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Produce a set of per-device 'delta' performance profiles (A100/H100/L40S/MI300) that describe expected latency, p50/p95 variance, and quantization sensitivity for new model builds, and define an automated pin-decay policy that safely relaxes strict version pins over time while preserving SLOs. Scope includes: (1) measurement harness updates, (2) delta profile schema and publishing pipeline, (3) pin-decay algorithm and rollout automation, (4) dashboards and alerting for regressions, and (5) documentation for SRE/SE/PM teams.
acceptance_criteria:
1) For each target device (A100/H100/L40S/MI300) we can publish a delta profile containing p50/p95 latencies, cold vs warm comparisons, memory tail metrics, and quantization sensitivity score.
2) Pin-decay policy prototypes can be toggled per-model and will automatically move a model from 'pinned' -> 'soft-pin' -> 'un-pinned' based on configurable age and observed drift thresholds.
3) Alerts fire to #inference-ops when a newly un-pinned model shows >10% p95 regression vs baseline for two consecutive 12h windows.
4) Automation has an opt-out and manual re-pin flow with audit log entries for every automatic action.
5) Documentation and a short runbook exist: links in artifacts; engineers can reproduce measurement runs locally.
risk: Medium: false positives in automated unpin could expose customers to regressions; measurement noise across SKUs (esp. MI300 cold-start variance) could cause churn. Mitigations: conservative thresholds, minimum sample windows, and canary groups before global policy application.
plan_summary: Week 1: extend perf harness to capture cold/warm, memory tail, and quant-sensitivity; Week 2: implement delta profile schema + publisher; Week 3: implement pin-decay microservice and simple state machine; Week 4: integrate dashboarding, alerts, and runbook; Week 5: internal canary and rollout.
